subject: Select2 and DT_Bootstrap in one Shiny web app

messages.author: 0b8f6965356502a5
messages.subject: Select2 and DT_Bootstrap in one Shiny web app
parts:
This is a follow-up to at least three group discussions about extending existing Javascript controls within the Shiny framework, namely Select2 and DataTable (Bootstrap). I wanted to write this to give something back to the group as so many others have helped significantly grow the Shiny tools.

This is a summary of the following discussions:
https://groups.google.com/forum/?fromgroups=#!topic/shiny-discuss/Fonr8vtOfpk
https://groups.google.com/forum/?fromgroups=#!topic/shiny-discuss/T4NL74DtDdI
https://groups.google.com/forum/?fromgroups=#!topic/shiny-discuss/K8LiWIM1ras

To begin with, I am a total Javascript and CSS newbie, so anyone that has significant skills in these areas, please feel free to make corrections with this post. If you are reading this and have no knowledge of Javascript or CSS and want to utilize these tools quickly in your Shiny webapp, then this might be quite helpful to you.

To be honest, the way I have been able to get these tools to work within Shiny feels a little brittle, but they work. Very little of what i have done is original work or code. The DataTable code was plagiarized from an earlier post by Haider Ali and the Select2 code was plagiarized from a recent post by Joe Cheng. I just want to give credit where credit is due.

One thing to note in the DataTable implementation. I hardcoded the value 'table' in the "$(document).ready" function at the end of the DT_Bootstrap.js file. I think this means all tables in the app will default to DT_Bootstrap tables, but I am not sure. I also extended the reactiveDataTable function to include the ID/name of the table as a parameter. The DataTable functionality also requires the xtable and stringer packages.

This example also uses the "actionButton" from the ShinyIncubator package.

To run the example, just unzip and issue a "runApp" command to the directory.
